title: 7-Day Rolling Average of Story Points Completed
prompt: Your team tracks daily story point completion in each sprint. Calculate a 7-day rolling average of `points_completed` for each day, ordered by `completion_date`. The rolling average should include the current day and the 6 preceding days (or fewer if fewer than 7 days of history exist). Return columns `completion_date` and `rolling_avg_points` (rounded to 2 decimal places). Order the result by `completion_date` ascending. Note that early rows will have partial windows (fewer than 7 days), and later rows should reflect the full 7-day trailing window.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE daily_completions (completion_date DATE NOT NULL, points_completed INTEGER NOT NULL);

composite_moves: time-window: Apply ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW frame to AVG(points_completed) partitioned by nothing, ordered by completion_date

hints: You need a window function that computes an average over a sliding frame of rows.
Use AVG() with an ORDER BY completion_date and a ROWS BETWEEN clause that includes the current row and the 6 preceding rows.
The frame clause is ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW, and you'll want to ROUND the result to 2 decimal places.
answer_key: SELECT completion_date, ROUND(AVG(points_completed) OVER (ORDER BY completion_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS rolling_avg_points FROM daily_completions ORDER BY completion_date;

_meta.scenario: a project management tool tracking sprint completion and task throughput
